Draw availability points from the detection surface

Source: R/sample_available.R
sample_available.Rd

For each animal, detected bin and presence draw, draws n cells from the whole water body that the array could detect the animal in: in proportion to the probability that the bin is detected from each cell, or uniformly over the cells at or above a minimum probability. The draws are the available half of a used-available design whose used half is sample_locations(). positionR 1.x drew availability from the detection surface of the array too (sample_points_from_system_de()); the differences are listed under Details.

Usage

sample_available(
  presence,
  coverage,
  grid,
  n,
  uniform_above = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

presence

The used points: a data frame with one row per animal, bin and draw and the columns animal_id (character), bin_start (POSIXct, UTC), draw (whole numbers), x and y (in the units of grid), such as the output of sample_locations() or true positions sampled by hand. A cell column, if given, must hold the cell of x and y on grid.

coverage

A data frame with the columns date (Date), cell (cells of grid) and p (0 to 1), one row per date and cell, such as the table of system_de().

grid

The SpatRaster whose cells coverage indexes, such as the lake raster the field was built on.

n

Number of available cells per stratum (animal, bin and draw).

uniform_above

NULL to draw cells in proportion to p; or one number in 0 to 1 to draw uniformly among the cells with p at or above it.

seed

An integer seed for the draws, or NULL to use the current random number stream. The caller's stream is restored afterwards when a seed is given.

Value

A data frame with n rows per kept stratum: animal_id, bin_start, draw (the presence draw the row is matched to), cell, and x and y, the cell centre. Attributes: "estimand"; "uniform_above"

and "n" as given; "epsg", the EPSG code of grid; and "dropped", one row per dropped stratum with animal_id, bin_start, draw and reason.

Details

Weighted (uniform_above = NULL). Cells are the rows of coverage on the bin's UTC date with p above 0, drawn with replacement in proportion to p. Presence points exist only for detected bins, and a bin is detected more often where the array hears well. If an animal uses cell x in proportion to u(x), and its bin is detected from x with probability d(x), the presence draws follow u(x) d(x). Availability drawn in proportion to d(x) carries the same factor, so it cancels in the ratio of used to available.

Which coverage. Pass the probability that a bin is detected: system_de() with transmissions set to the transmissions a tag sends in one bin (24 an hour at a 150 s mean delay). An hour is a presence when the animal was heard at least once in it, so that is the filter the presence points went through. The per-transmission table weights by a different event. On Stoney Lake, 20 simulated animals with no depth preference on 70 receivers gave, with the per-transmission weight, -0.091 per m of bottom depth (95% CI -0.161 to -0.020) on their true tracks and -0.065 (-0.123 to -0.008) from position draws; with the hourly weight, -0.032 (-0.090 to 0.026) and -0.010 (-0.057 to 0.038). These are the means over the animals of block 1 at beta 0 in stoney_selection$trial, with t intervals. On that array the hourly weight is close to uniform: 77.7% of cell-days are detected with probability 0.95 or more in an hour.

Uniform (uniform_above = 0.1, say). Cells are the rows of coverage on the bin's date with p at or above uniform_above, drawn uniformly. With the per-transmission table of system_de() and 0.1 this follows the example of positionR 1.x, which kept the cells strictly above 0.1. It cuts away water the array barely hears, so used points there have no available counterpart. uniform_above = 0 takes every row of coverage, including cells no receiver can hear; leave out the rows of cells you do not count as available, such as water cut off from the receivers, before the call.

Differences from positionR 1.x. sample_points_from_system_de() weighted each cell by the chance, for one transmission, that one or more receivers detect it (cumulative_prob), kept cells strictly above a minimum of 0.001 and strictly below an optional maximum. With a surface carrying fish and time columns it drew one set per fish and time period; with a template of positions and a surface without those columns, it sampled once and copied that one set to every fish and time period. This function weights by the coverage table it is given (hourly, with 24 transmissions, in the article), has no minimum or maximum, keeps cells with p >= uniform_above in the uniform mode, and draws one set per presence draw.

Why the whole water body. Availability drawn from a disc round each bin's position can show selection the animals do not have on Stoney Lake: cells with more water within reach are deeper offshore, so a walk with no preference looks like avoidance of deep water. Northrup et al. (2013) found the same kind of bias in simulations when the spatial extent of availability was set wrongly. The coefficient from the whole water body is a lake-scale one, of where in the water body the animal spent its detected bins against where the array could have heard it. vignette("habitat-selection") sets it against the true track.

Each presence draw gets its own n cells. A stratum (one animal, bin and draw) is therefore one matched set of one used and n available points, and the strata of one draw index form a full data set, as multiple imputation over the presence draws needs. A stratum with no cell to draw, because coverage has no row on its date or none that qualifies, is dropped, counted in a warning and listed in the attribute dropped.

Left to the user: the coverage table, the mode and the model. used_available() stacks the used and available points with covariates read at each cell, and fits nothing.

References

Northrup, J. M., Hooten, M. B., Anderson, C. R. and Wittemyer, G. (2013). Practical guidance on characterizing availability in resource selection functions under a use-availability design. Ecology, 94, 1456-1463. doi:10.1890/12-1688.1

See also

sample_locations() for the used points, system_de() for the weight, used_available() to stack the two.

Examples

tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield")
grid <- terra::rast(tif)
# Beyond 2 km the Stoney curve is below 0.001 at every receiver; leaving
# those pairs out keeps the example quick.
dist <- water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers, max_distance = 2000)
model <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
field <- de_field(dist, de_model(model, sigma = list(station_hour = 0)))
#> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.
counts <- bin_detections(stoney_track$detections, stoney_track$receivers,
                         stoney_track$tags)
surface <- location_surface(counts, field)
presence <- sample_locations(surface, n = 20, seed = 1)
# Every receiver listens on each day of the study
days <- unique(as.Date(presence$bin_start, tz = "UTC"))
listening <- expand.grid(station_id = stoney_track$receivers$station_id,
                         date = days, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# Weighted by the probability that an hour is detected: 24 transmissions
hourly <- system_de(field, listening, transmissions = 24)
available <- sample_available(presence, hourly, grid, n = 20, seed = 1)
head(available)
#>   animal_id           bin_start draw  cell      x       y
#> 1 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1  4826 732454 4939091
#> 2 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1  6432 725054 4938091
#> 3 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1  8293 726354 4936991
#> 4 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1 17329 722754 4931591
#> 5 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1  3831 733754 4939691
#> 6 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1 16983 721754 4931791
# Uniform over the cells heard with probability 0.1 or more per transmission
per_transmission <- system_de(field, listening)
uniform <- sample_available(presence, per_transmission, grid, n = 20,
                            uniform_above = 0.1, seed = 1)
nrow(uniform) / nrow(presence)
#> [1] 20
